title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
slides: Meta wants your news without paying for it?
New terms let Meta train AI on news sites
But publishers may not realize they opted in
News sites can still opt out before deadline
Check your site's settings today, or lose leverage
thread_text:
1. Meta's Quiet Power Grab

New terms let Meta train AI on news sites — and many publishers don't realize they've already opted in.

2. Opted In By Default

Meta added this clause deep in updated policies. Silence equals consent, and most newsrooms missed it entirely.

3. Publishers Left in the Dark

Editors are now scrambling to check their settings after the deadline quietly locked in their content for AI training.

4. The Leverage You Lose

Once your content trains Meta's models, you've handed over your archive for free. No royalties, no credit, no control.

5. Check Your Settings Now

Go to your site's Meta business settings and opt out before the deadline. What happens if you don't?

instagram.caption:
If you run a news site, your archive may already be training Meta's AI — for free.

Meta slipped a clause into its updated terms: silence counts as consent, so publishers who never replied got opted in by default.

No royalties, no credit, no control over how your articles feed the models.

There's still time to opt out in your Meta business settings before the deadline.

Miss it, and you lose all leverage over content you paid to produce. 📰

Check your settings today, before the window closes. ⏳

Have you looked at yours yet — or did you, like most newsrooms, miss it entirely? 👀
